summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB 10.6 Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3) on RHEL 7.9. Since RHEL 7 is EOL for the official MariaDB repo tooling and had no base OS repo configured, I manually pointed yum at the MariaDB archive (archive.mariadb.org, mariadb-10.6/rhel7-amd64) plus a CentOS 7 vault base repo (node3 only, for missing perl/libaio/boost deps), installed MariaDB-server + galera-4, opened firewalld ports 3306/4567/4568/4444, and wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and rsync-based SST. Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, then started node2 and node3 which joined via SST, reaching a 3-node Synced/Primary cluster. Verified multi-master write propagation (writes from each of the 3 nodes visible on the others). Demonstrated availability during a member outage: stopped node3, confirmed the cluster stayed Primary at cluster_size=2, wrote a row via node1, restarted node3, and confirmed it automatically resynced (IST) back to Synced/cluster_size=3 with the row present. Then executed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id + wsrep health on all 3 nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially via `systemctl reboot` (one at a time, quorum preserved throughout — never below 2/3), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed each node's mariadb.service was active and rejoined the cluster (Synced/Primary/size=3) before moving to the next. A final post-restart write/read check across all three nodes confirmed the cluster still works end-to-end. Root and SST credentials were generated on-node and only ever passed via secret_env in later commands (not left in final report).
actions_performed: Investigated OS (RHEL 7.9) and lack of any configured yum repos on all 3 nodes
Configured MariaDB 10.6 archive yum repo (archive.mariadb.org/mariadb-10.6/yum/rhel7-amd64) with imported GPG key on node1, node2, node3
Added CentOS 7 vault base repo on node3 to satisfy perl/libaio/boost-program-options dependencies missing from the base image
Installed MariaDB-server, MariaDB-client, galera-4, rsync on all 3 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all 3 nodes
Appended CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on all 3 nodes
Generated SST and root passwords on node1 and wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and node-specific wsrep_node_address/name on all 3 nodes
Bootstrapped Galera on node1 via galera_new_cluster; set root password and created sst_user via SQL
Started mariadb on node2 and node3, confirmed both joined via SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary
Verified multi-master write propagation with inserts from node1, node2, node3 all visible cluster-wide
Enabled mariadb.service on boot on all 3 nodes
Captured healthy baseline (wsrep status + service active) on all 3 nodes before disruption
Stopped mariadb on node3, verified cluster stayed Primary at size=2 and accepted a write via node1 that replicated to node2
Restarted mariadb on node3, verified automatic IST resync back to size=3/Synced/Primary with the during-outage row present
Captured baseline boot_id (kernel random boot_id) plus wsrep health on all 3 nodes for the restart protocol
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned pre-disconnect), one at a time, preserving 2/3 quorum throughout

Polled each node until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart, and confirmed mariadb.service active + cluster rejoined (Synced/Primary/size=3) before restarting the next node
Ran a final post-all-restarts write/read validation across all 3 nodes confirming continued multi-master replication
Dropped test databases (galtest, finaltest) used for validation

evidence.requirement: 3-member Galera cluster established; writes through any member visible from the others
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped, node2/node3 joined reaching cluster_size=3/Synced/Primary; inserts made from node2, node1, and node3 were each visible on the other two members

evidence.requirement: Database stays available with one member down; that member auto-resyncs on return
evidence.summary: Stopped node3 (baseline Synced captured first); cluster remained Primary at size=2 and accepted/replicated a write via node1; node3 restarted and automatically resynced to size=3/Synced with the during-outage row present

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d72bd4ec.../Synced captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; post-restart boot_id bf08c354... (changed); mariadb active and cluster size=3/Synced/Primary after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 809708f3.../Synced captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 537fec0c... (changed); mariadb active and cluster size=3/Synced/Primary after restart

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 73bafeef.../Synced captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 27da3e81... (changed); mariadb active and cluster size=3/Synced/Primary, all 3 wsrep_incoming_addresses present after restart

evidence.requirement: End-to-end functionality confirmed after all three sequential restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart write from node1 was visible on node2 and node3, and a subsequent write from node2 was visible on node3, confirming multi-master replication still functions after the full restart cycle
